findings.evidence: Lines 71-85 of the new file (`(semisimplePart k H K g, unipotentPart k H K g)`, both projection proofs `(rfl)`); `grep -rn "jordanDecomposition" TauCeti` shows the point-level name occurs only in its own definition, its two rfl lemmas, and the module docstring.
findings.fix: Delete `jordanDecomposition`, `jordanDecomposition_fst`, and `jordanDecomposition_snd`; users write the pair directly. If a pair-level name is wanted, it should come with a point-level uniqueness lemma (the analogue of `eq_jordanDecomposition_iff`) that makes it more than sugar.
findings.issue: `jordanDecomposition` is by definition `(semisimplePart k H K g, unipotentPart k H K g)`, with `jordanDecomposition_fst`/`_snd` proved by `rfl` and no consumer in the PR or repo — a second spelling of the same pair. Unlike `TauCeti.GeneralLinearGroup.jordanDecomposition` (LinearAlgebra/JordanChevalley/Multiplicative.lean:190), which is the primitive `Classical.choose` term with `jordanDecomposition_spec` (:196) and `eq_jordanDecomposition_iff` (:205) giving it content, this one carries no characterization.

summary: The Tannakian lift of the linear Jordan factors to group points is new material and reuses the located Tannaka and Jordan–Chevalley API correctly. Only `jordanDecomposition` is redundant: it is a contentless second spelling of the pair of the two parts defined immediately above it.
